headline: Inside the dragon kiln
notes: Leave the drawn chamber unobstructed and place the selected part’s label on its own ruled strip immediately below.
detail: Follow the rising chamber from the lower firebox to the chimney at the uphill end.

headline: Plan your visit
notes: Use a perforated address card as the destination landmark beside the native visit-route picker.
detail: Find 85 Lorong Tawas and choose the right route for an independent visit, a group or a workshop.

headline: The clay studio
notes: Frame the wheel and hand-building studies as offset arches with a linked caption beneath each one.
detail: See how shaping clay on a turning wheel differs from working the material by hand.

headline: Teachers’ field notes
notes: Put the model classroom question on a lifted margin sheet next to the lesson introduction.
detail: Use a bowl to help pupils separate an observation from a claim that needs evidence.

headline: At the potter’s wheel
notes: Pair an edge-to-edge monochrome hand study with short numbered gesture strips that open independently.
detail: Follow a potter through centring, opening, lifting and shaping a vessel.

headline: Wood & ember
notes: Use embers as the dominant atmospheric field and attach a smaller glazed-surface sample to the opposite corner.
detail: Trace how fuel, moving ash and the finished surface connect inside a wood-fired kiln.

headline: Glaze library
notes: Give the rim image an inspection frame with a visible control that changes magnification within the same crop.
detail: Look closely at a green rim and compare the clay body, glaze and traces of wood ash.

headline: A family visit
notes: Tuck a readable clue card against the illustrated forms so a child and a companion can study the object together.
detail: Pick a shape, follow its outline with your eyes and ask someone else what they see.

headline: In good company
notes: Make the 15-person heritage-tour threshold the strongest numerical element and keep the group-size field beside its guidance.
detail: Check the tour minimum or collect the details for a private workshop enquiry.

headline: The heritage journal
notes: Run the three dated sources across a double-rule masthead above an illustrated ceramics feature.
detail: Read the records behind the kiln’s construction, the Tan family business and the heritage award.

headline: Kiln lexicon
notes: Set the real initials from the dictionary in a typesetter’s grid with the search field visible alongside.
detail: Find an unfamiliar kiln or pottery term by its first letter or by a word in the definition.

headline: The vessel cabinet
notes: Present the three vessel studies at an equal scale and reveal one distinguishing contour per form.
detail: Compare the bowl’s broad rim, the jar’s curved shoulder and the cup’s flared side.

headline: Field sketchbook
notes: Tilt the sheet slightly against a ruled binding edge and keep the printable download at its foot.
detail: Take a printable contour exercise or save a short written observation about a vessel.

headline: A slow afternoon
notes: Use an arched light study opposite a three-stop route strip that leads to the setting, kiln and vessels.
detail: Take a self-paced look at light, slope and form at three suggested stops.

headline: The visitor desk
notes: Treat the visit, class and history choices as service-counter signs above a clear grid of official destinations.
detail: Choose the operator’s directions, workshop information or history by the purpose of your visit.

headline: How the kiln breathes
notes: For an alternate anatomy plate, set the entire elevation on a cool drawing board and align the three labels like drafting keys.
detail: Read the head, climbing chamber and chimney in one continuous elevation.

headline: What can a bowl tell us?
notes: Replace the ruled spread in this alternate with three upright enquiry cards arranged beside a still life of unfinished vessels.
detail: Ask the class to name one visible detail, one possible explanation and one question for the maker.

headline: Read the surface
notes: Crop the green rim across the cover and pin a pale specimen slip to the lower edge for an alternative close-reading layout.
detail: Start with a reflected highlight and work outward to the coating and the clay beneath it.

headline: Three dates at Lorong Tawas
notes: Use a vertical filing-tab composition for the source dates and an unglazed still life as the archive’s object study.
detail: Follow the dated evidence from the kiln’s construction to recognition of its living craft.

headline: Follow the afternoon light
notes: Fold the suggested walk into three panels, with a continuous sunlit wall tying the waypoints together.
detail: Start in a visitor area, look along the kiln’s slope and finish by observing a single vessel.
